answer.evidence: The object is a flat, front-facing signboard made of stacked rectangular panels (white, teal, yellow with a '4', grey) in a uniform 10px-wide silhouette from row 1 to 29. The width never changes, so there is no overhanging cap and no ellipse. The row 0 width of 8 is just a trimmed outline corner, not a cap. There is no front-edge line with eave shadow and no horizontal surface, so every part is a vertical face. This is a front elevation with no top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small bollard-style sign post: a pale top cap, a dark band, a light body with a yellow badge showing '4', and a dark base. It measures 12 visible tones per 16x16 tile, matching kiosk-a (12) and beating bus-shelter-a (6), though it is below vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 13%, a little above bus-shelter-a (9%) and kiosk-a/vending-a (0%), but the flat areas are small and broken up by the badge and shading bands. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines lean toward a tint of the adjacent material, as in the references. The ramps hold about 4 steps on the body, with a highlight edge and a shadow edge, close to the references on a thin object. A careful artist would accept it next to the references without it looking noticeably flatter or more sticker-like.

surfaces.part: top white panel of sign box

answer.evidence: The object is a flat rectangular sign post drawn face-on. The silhouette is 10 px wide for rows 1-29, with only row 0 slightly narrower (8) as an outline corner. There is no widening-then-narrowing ellipse cap, no front-edge line with eave shadow, and no visible contents. The top white panel (rows 1-6) is a vertical sign face, separated by dark outline rows at 0 and 7. Every segment (white, teal, yellow with the numeral 4, gray) is a vertical face stacked below the others. The cap is not wider than the shaft, so it does not overhang as the column kind requires.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a slim bollard-style sign post with a yellow-gold body, a dark cap and base, and a number '4' on a dark panel. Its measured facts sit within the reference range: 12 visible tones per tile (kiosk-a 12, vending-a 20, bus-shelter-a 6), 13% near-flat coverage (bus-shelter-a 9%, the others 0%), and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted and not a black sticker line. By eye, the body has about 4 lightness steps: highlight edge, mid, shade side, and dark cap/base. It has only a little grain, and the number panel and the vertical body are fairly smooth. Compared with vending-a and kiosk-a, which carry more clustered detail and varied panels, it looks somewhat thinner and flatter. Since it is a thin single-tile prop, sparseness alone is not a failure. It is, however, a bit plain next to the richer references, and it sits closer to bus-shelter-a's simplicity than to the best references. When in doubt, fail.
